limitations: In this Windows x64 run, the production default timer resumed 3.05ms and 5.54ms after its absolute deadline; the latest key samples were already 12.97ms and 11.03ms old. The monitor therefore returned key_state_unavailable for both fake held and fake released states under its 5ms timer-lateness and sample-freshness bound.

The real Electron run verifies fail-closed cancellation and timer cleanup but does not establish a real-time released cutoff continuing preparation or sending selectionBudgetMs=0. Exact-cutoff and 5ms jitter branches pass deterministic fake-clock fixtures; a delayed sample older than one poll interval or a timer more than one interval late fails closed.

An independent review found that a released sample up to 5ms before cutoff cannot prove there was no key re-press after that sample and before cutoff. If preparation finishes after a later release, the current key check and helper zero-budget check may observe released state and continue. The polling-only implementation therefore does not prove exact held-at-cutoff semantics; this is a P1 acceptance gap.
No real key state, BrowserWindow, native helper, OS clipboard, panel side effect, physical input, or target-visible paste was exercised.
The existing 8000ms image-preparation deadline scenario uses a pending monitor stub so its timer does not supersede that separate worker-timeout case.

independentReview.scope: Read-only review of selection-key cutoff, sample freshness, jitter and cutoff-to-helper behavior.
independentReview.finding: A fresh released pre-cutoff sample does not rule out a re-press held at cutoff. The current level-state polling API has no key transition timestamp to reconstruct that event.
independentReview.effect: Keep exact held-at-cutoff acceptance open; this probe and its fakes do not close the gap.
